race.office: Governor of Arizona (joint ticket with lieutenant governor)

nominee.t: Republican nominee. Won the July 21, 2026 four-way primary (earlier co-endorsed with Karrin Taylor Robson by Trump in April 2025; Robson withdrew Feb 12, 2026), beating Rep. David Schweikert by about 60 points in unofficial results. Running mate: Sine Kerr, Buckeye dairy farmer, state senator 2018–2025, named Arizona state executive director of the USDA Farm Service Agency in May 2025.

ballot.t: He is not on the 2026 AZ-05 House ballot; the seat is open. See az-races.json.

oneliner.t: Republican U.S. representative for Arizona's 5th District since 2017, former Arizona Senate president and House Freedom Caucus chair (2019–2022), now the Trump-endorsed GOP nominee for governor.

hometown.t: Tucson, Arizona (born there); has lived in Gilbert for decades per his campaign

upbringing.t: Andrew Steven Biggs was born in Tucson. As a young man he served a Latter-day Saints mission to Japan and became fluent in Japanese. He earned a B.A. in Asian studies at Brigham Young University (1982), married Cindy Biggs that year, and earned a law degree at the University of Arizona (1984). He practiced at a firm in Hobbs, New Mexico, then became a prosecutor in Phoenix. In 1993 he won $10 million in the American Family Publishers sweepstakes. The couple have six children; a daughter, Cosette, died of cancer in 2025.

career.role: Attorney (firm in Hobbs, N.M.), then prosecutor in Phoenix
U.S. Representative, AZ-05; Freedom Caucus chair 2019–2022

platform.t: Eliminate the state income tax; work with localities to cut property taxes; end what he calls Hobbs's anti-homebuilding policies; stop Wall Street from buying homes; reduce reliance on California fuel; pursue nuclear power.
Review every agency for waste, fraud and abuse (a DOGE-style effort); notice and disclosure rules for the State Protocol Fund; ban foreign money in campaigns and initiatives.
Reintroduce a Border Strike Force; encourage local participation in the federal 287(g) immigration-enforcement program; fully resource DPS and school security.

Fight for Arizona's Colorado River allocation; long-term water strategy via WIFA; measure aquifers; desalination, recycling and Bartlett Dam storage; repeal Hobbs's executive order prioritizing wind and solar on state land; promote mining.
End state incentives and subsidies; require data centers not to draw power or water away from homes and businesses; leave zoning to localities.
Protect Empowerment Scholarship Accounts; opt into the federal education tax credit; emphasize core academics and trade pathways.

'Make Arizona Healthy Again' agenda: end medical mandates, over-the-counter ivermectin, raw-milk sales, SNAP junk-food limits. Says there is significant Medicaid fraud, especially among able-bodied single adults.
Sign election bills Hobbs vetoed; speed up results; ensure only eligible citizens vote.

promises.t: Phase out / eliminate the state income tax.
Review every state agency and program for waste, fraud and abuse.
End state incentives for data centers.
Repeal Hobbs's executive order prioritizing wind and solar on state land.
Reintroduce a Border Strike Force and encourage 287(g) participation.
Start work on inauguration day instead of soliciting inauguration-fund contributions.
Create a 'Make Arizona Healthy Again' Governor's Advisory Council.

claims.claim: Elected in 2016 to represent Arizona's Fifth District.

record.t: Won the 2016 GOP primary by 16 votes over Christine Jones and the general with 64.1%.

claims.claim: Served two years as Chairman of the House Freedom Caucus.

record.t: Chair from Oct 1, 2019 to Jan 1, 2022, per Wikipedia's infobox (succeeding Mark Meadows).

claims.claim: Served eight years in the Arizona House and six years in the Arizona Senate.

said.where: campaign 'Meet Andy' page; also 2026 Clean Elections statement

claims.claim: Elected Arizona State Senate President in 2012.

record.t: Served as Senate President 2013–2017, consistent with election by the chamber after the 2012 elections.

claims.claim: Lifetime ratings of 100% from Club for Growth and National Right to Life, 100% NumbersUSA, 97% ACU, 93% Heritage Action.

record.t: The scorecards were not opened. His 2021 House bio listed slightly different figures (Heritage Action 95%, NumbersUSA 99%), so the numbers vary by date.

claims.claim: Has six children and twelve grandchildren; married to Cindy and living in Gilbert for over 35 years.

record.t: Wikipedia confirms the 1982 marriage and six children but lists eleven grandchildren (the count can change). Gilbert residency length was not independently checked. His 2025 House disclosure lists a Gilbert, AZ property as a rental property; it is not established whether that is his residence.

Hobbs vetoed a bipartisan housing-supply bill in March 2024, calling it 'a step too far.' She has also signed housing bills that passed with Republican support, per Phoenix New Times. 'Anti-homebuilding' is a characterization.

claims.claim: Hobbs vetoed a requirement that state contract bidders disclose political contributions.

record.t: KJZZ reports Hobbs vetoed Sen. TJ Shope's disclosure bills, and AG Mayes said the Sunshine case shows a need for reform on contractor donations.

claims.claim: Hobbs vetoed rules for paid and out-of-state signature collectors; Arizona's overdose death rate rose last year; Hobbs issued an executive order prioritizing wind and solar on state land; Hobbs vetoed election-integrity bills.

record.t: Not checked against veto records, CDC/ADHS overdose data or the executive order text in this pass.

said.where: Biggs for Arizona TV ads (aired spring 2026; spend unknown)

record.t: Phoenix New Times found the campaign's evidence (spending, solar/wind reliance) thin. Arizona differs sharply from California: right-to-work, low flat income tax, lower education and social spending. Republicans have controlled the Legislature, which negotiates budgets with her.

claims.claim: Hobbs is 'going on secret foreign trips.'

said.where: 'We Can't Trust Katie Hobbs' TV ad

record.t: The trip was a publicly reported two-day April trip to a Diamondbacks game in Mexico City, led and paid for by the Arizona Hispanic Chamber of Commerce. Ticket costs first came from the state protocol fund, which she said she would reimburse.

claims.claim: Asked who paid for her travel, Hobbs said 'It's none of your business.'

said.where: 'We Can't Trust Katie Hobbs' TV ad

record.t: She did say it to a woman at the Mexico City event, then apologized, saying the public has a right to know who paid. The ad omits the apology.

Phoenix New Times argues federal policy (tariffs, the Iran war's fuel effects) drives much of the cost increase and that the housing shortage predates her, while noting housing is partly a state issue.

said.t: In the governor's debate said his past opposition to Medicaid expansion rested on predicted cost overruns, and alleged significant fraud among able-bodied single adults.

did.t: Was one of 36 Republican legislators who joined the Goldwater Institute's 2013 lawsuit against Arizona's Medicaid expansion. Courts ruled against them in 2015 and on appeal on Mar 16, 2017.

promises_prev.promise: Reduce the national debt, balance the federal budget and cut wasteful spending (2018 Ballotpedia candidate survey)

evidence.t: He has pushed spending offsets, e.g., a Feb 2024 bill to pay for $17.6B in Israel security aid by repealing the IRS/Commerce funds created in the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act (not enacted). No balanced-budget enactment was found.

complicating.t: A House member cannot deliver this alone. Federal debt totals during his tenure and his budget-bill votes are not tallied here; votes are in the separate key-vote file. Phoenix New Times notes he voted for the 2025 federal budget legislation.

entries.t: Offered an NDAA amendment affirming 'unflinching support' for Israel.
Supports Israel aid but insists it be offset; introduced a $17.6B offset supplemental.
Agrees with Hobbs on a moratorium on new incentives ('enough incentives to come to Arizona anyway').
End all state tax breaks and subsidies for data centers.
Joined the lawsuit against Arizona's Medicaid expansion.
Says opposition was cost-based; alleges fraud; warns ~$18B in federal AHCCCS funds were put at risk by delayed audit filings (not verified).

aipac_endorse.t: Not confirmed — Track AIPAC lists AIPAC among the groups that funded him but does not label it an endorsement; AIPAC's own endorsement page was not checked (as of 2026-10-08).

aipac_pac.note: career — Track AIPAC's $39,184 total combines AIPAC and GCSC and is not split; see 'others'.

udp.note: Track AIPAC shows $0 in pro-Israel independent expenditures (data 7/5/26).

others.name: Track AIPAC career 'Israel lobby total' (direct donations; groups listed: AIPAC, GCSC)

israel.votes_note: Roll calls are handled in the separate key-vote file. Wikipedia notes he voted to support Israel after the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack.

statements.t: Called Israel a longtime friend and key partner against Iran; filed an NDAA amendment affirming U.S. support.
Called Israel America's greatest ally; introduced the Fiscally Responsible Israel Supplemental Act ($17.6B, offset) and opposed a 'clean' unoffset package.

fec.cid: H6AZ05083 (federal House ID; governor committee is state-registered)
fec.committee: Biggs for Arizona (state committee); federal: Biggs for Congress C00610451, leadership PAC Building Innovative Good Government Solutions PAC C00633164
fec.src_note: Q2 2026: raised about $916,700, spent $770,000, ending cash about $1.2M (Arizona Mirror; KTAR says $1.27M with no debt). KJZZ says he spent $2.4M winning the primary. His campaign said on Jul 16 it had raised $2.7M total with $1.1M on hand (campaign claim; date basis unclear). KTAR says donors were mostly small-dollar, many under $50, largely retirees. Cycle total receipts are not set because no independent figure was found.

support: Turning Point PAC — $458,000 for Biggs before the primary (KJZZ); Axios reports it paid Sen. Jake Hoffman's firm 1Ten LLC about $1.5M to help elect Biggs and defeat Hobbs (figures may overlap)
oppose: Democratic Governors Association — $10M pledged for Hobbs (Jul 28, 2026)

fec.outside_note: The RGA had not committed money as of late July; AZ Family (Sep 8) said Biggs was 'expected' to get a seven-figure ad buy, source unnamed. Funders of Turning Point PAC and the DGA were not retrieved.

money_history.office: U.S. House committee (not on 2026 House ballot)
money_history.note: No transfer to a state campaign shown.

money2.note: No named donors in coverage read. The leadership PAC's (C00633164) history was not pulled.

corp.t: His FEC committee took PAC ('other committee') money every House cycle: $227,400.50 (2016), $311,427 (2018), $363,780 (2020), $93,550 (2022), $75,985.20 (2024), $7,000 (2025–26). FEC's summary does not split business/trade from ideological/leadership PACs. Turning Point PAC, an ideological group, is spending to defeat Hobbs and elect Biggs; Axios reports that Sen. Jake Hoffman's companies, including 1Ten LLC, which received Turning Point PAC money, have been paid about $1.5 million for that effort. Turning Point PAC's total for this race and its funders were not retrieved.

lobby.t: Track AIPAC lists $39,184 in career pro-Israel direct donations (AIPAC and GCSC), with $0 in independent expenditures.

networth.note: Computed from the CY2025 annual report: assets $2,019,008–$10,111,000 (excluding a state pension of undetermined value) minus liabilities $530,003–$1,100,000. The two largest assets are an Alexandria, Va. residential property and a Gilbert, Ariz. rental property, each listed at $1M–$5M. Liabilities: a mortgage on the Alexandria second home ($500K–$1M), a co-signed student loan, and a personal loan from Frank and Trisha Groe ($15K–$50K each). Quiver Quantitative showed no estimate.

note.t: Income: rent from the two properties, an Arizona State Retirement System pension ($14,712), and minor book-sales income from Free Man Press. No foreign assets or income. Earlier years' reports were not reviewed for trades.

committees: Judiciary (campaign says he chairs the Crime and Federal Government Surveillance Subcommittee — not verified)
effectiveness.note: At the Oct 6 debate he cited the AMBER Alert in Indian Country Act, the JACK Act and Right to Try as bipartisan bills he helped advance. Sponsored and enacted counts were not retrieved from congress.gov. A third-party aggregator lists about 896 sponsored measures across the 115th–119th Congresses, which is unverified.

democracy.t: Voted Yea on the objection to Arizona's electoral votes (Roll Call 10; failed 121–303).
Voted Yea on the objection to Pennsylvania's electoral votes (Roll Call 11; failed 138–282). The Clerk's page does not name the state; Ballotpedia identifies it as Pennsylvania with the same tally.

Among 126 House Republicans who signed the amicus brief backing Texas v. Pennsylvania, which the Supreme Court rejected. Earlier in 2020 he appeared in a video with Rep. Paul Gosar claiming widespread fraud and calling for an audit of Maricopa County's count.

Spoke at 'Stop the Steal' rallies. Organizer Ali Alexander testified to the Jan 6 committee that he spoke with Biggs in person beforehand. Biggs denied Rolling Stone's report that he helped plan the events, and he blamed antifa for the Capitol attack.

Then-Arizona House Speaker Rusty Bowers testified (June 21, 2022) that Biggs called him the morning of Jan 6 to press him to decertify Arizona's electors. Witnesses at the June 23, 2022 hearing said Biggs had sought a presidential pardon related to the certification.

Subpoenaed by the Jan 6 committee (May 12, 2022) and refused to comply. On Dec 19, 2022 the committee unanimously referred him, with McCarthy, Jordan and Perry, to the House Ethics Committee; no Ethics Committee outcome is reported in sources read.
His campaign's announcement article describes him as having supported failed efforts to overturn Trump's 2020 loss.

debates.note: Debated Hourihan at the Oct 6, 2026 Clean Elections debate; Hobbs declined.

note.t: Born in Tucson (1958). He left the state for BYU, an LDS mission in Japan and early law practice in New Mexico, so continuous years are not computed. He has lived in Gilbert for decades per his campaign.

checks.legal: CourtListener and Justia were not reached (outside this tool's provenance set). News, Wikipedia and Ballotpedia were searched. No criminal charges or civil judgments against Biggs were found. The Jan 6 committee's Ethics referral (2022) is recorded under democracy because it is a referral, not a finding. ethics.house.gov was not opened directly.
checks.foreign: CY2025 House financial disclosure read directly: no foreign assets or income. FARA was not searched.
checks.claims: Mechanical sample: (a) every checkable claim on the 'Meet Andy' page (2016 election, Freedom Caucus chair, 8/6 legislative years, Senate President 2012, Arizona native, ratings, family/Gilbert; committee/subcommittee and law-license claims not rated); (b) the first 10 claims on the Issues page (1 partly, 2 true, 5/6/8/10 grouped as unverifiable; 3, 4, 7 and 9 are promises); (c) ad spending is unknown, so I used the two ads covered by Phoenix New Times (the minute-long spot and 'We Can't Trust Katie Hobbs').
checks.democracy: Jan 2021 objection roll calls read directly on clerk.house.gov (Roll Calls 10 and 11). He took office Jan 3, 2017; no House vote on an objection occurred at the Jan 6, 2017 count. Statements and the Jan 6 committee record via Wikipedia. No search for statements on the 2024 results.

recordx.note: Disclosure: CY2025 annual report filed May 13, 2026, before the May 15 deadline. FEC: the 2019–20 committee page showed no RFAI or notices; other cycles' notice tables did not render, so 'clean' is partial. Missed-vote % not obtained. A third-party sample showed 22 of his last 50 votes as Not Voting during the governor's race (unofficial).

research_notes: MONEY: FEC read directly for every House cycle (2016, 2018 and 2024 candidate pages; 2020, 2022 and 2026 committee pages). The 2024 committee page was refused by the fetch proxy (HTTP 429, rate-limited), so 2024 comes from the candidate page instead (matches Ballotpedia). Track AIPAC read directly. money_history stays 'news' because the state governor filings (seethemoney.az.gov blocked) and Turning Point PAC/DGA funders come only from news. State totals: Q2 raised $916.7K, COH ~$1.2M (Mirror) or $1.27M (KTAR); total cycle receipts unknown; $2.4M spent in the primary (KJZZ). Leadership PAC C00633164 not pulled. TURNING POINT/HOFFMAN: Axios reports ~$1.5M from Turning Point PAC to Sen. Jake Hoffman's 1Ten LLC to elect Biggs. Hoffman led a Senate probe of Hobbs and then handed it off. That is Hoffman's conduct; it is recorded as outside money, not as Biggs's act. Hoffman’s fake-electors case was dismissed without prejudice on Aug 11, 2026; no charges are pending, in the fake-electors case. PROMISES_PREV: thin. A full Congress promise-vs-record needs the key-vote file and Treasury debt data. CLAIMS: 14 entries — 6 true, 2 partly, 2 misleading, 1 opinion, 3 unverifiable (one groups Issues-page claims 5, 6, 8 and 10). Debate claims (660 million acre-feet storage; $18B AHCCCS funds at risk; 2017 cuts expanded the base) were not rated. EFFECTIVENESS: subcommittee chair claim and bill counts need congress.gov. Ethics referral outcome unknown. Photo not added.
